text: Removed the host.docker.internal extra_hosts mapping from plugin-runner in docker-compose.yml (July 2026). It is not needed: async plugin/coder callbacks reach the app via the Compose service name (http://app:3000/chat), not via the host gateway. The mapping landed on plugin-runner by accident — commit abb8b30 claimed to move it from the database service to the app service but actually moved it from app to plugin-runner. Do not re-add it to plugin-runner: plugin scripts run arbitrary code and the mapping gives them a route to services on the Docker host. If the app ever needs to reach a host-local LLM endpoint (custom baseUrl), add the mapping to the app service instead.

Baileys (@whiskeysockets/baileys) is pinned to an EXACT version in package.json, deliberately, with no caret or tilde. Do not 'tidy' it back to a range. Two reasons: upstream's 7.x prerelease tag naming is inconsistent (rc.9 vs rc14), so caret ranges over those prereleases resolve in surprising ways; and RC-to-RC releases have shipped real breaking changes (getPrivacyTokens renamed to issuePrivacyTokens, encryptMediaRetryRequest becoming synchronous). Because the library links a session to the owner's personal WhatsApp account, upgrades should be deliberate rather than automatic. package.json cannot hold a comment, which is why this is recorded here.

Related stance from the owner, decided during the rc.9 -> rc14 upgrade: if a Baileys upgrade invalidates the linked session in data/whatsapp, rescanning the QR code is the accepted fallback. Do not build session backup, migration, or auth-state-versioning plumbing for this; it is not worth the code. Baileys' useMultiFileAuthState on-disk format has been stable so far, but it is not a guarantee we defend in code.

The /settings/config editor applies changes by validating with parseConfig, writing config.toml (previous version kept as config.toml.bak), then process.exit(0) so Docker's restart policy reboots the app. Owner explicitly accepted: (1) saving kills any in-progress agent turn; (2) only the app restarts — plugin-runner, coder, signal-bridge, python-runner read config.toml at their own startup and need manual restarts (warned on the page); (3) structural validation only — a runtime-bad but valid config (wrong API key) can still crash-loop, recovery via config.toml.bak on the host; (4) the page shows raw secrets to any Basic-Auth-authenticated browser, consistent with the plugin config endpoint. In-process hot reload was rejected as too invasive: config values are consumed throughout startup (agent creation, Telegram webhook registration, WhatsApp init).

Pi 0.85.x introduced its own CredentialStore / Models.getAuth() orchestration for OAuth credentials. Decided (owner approved, Pi 0.80.6 -> 0.85.1 upgrade) NOT to adopt it: stavrobot keeps its own auth-file storage (src/auth.ts), expiry check and retry loop, and only calls Provider.auth.oauth.refresh/toAuth/login directly. Reason: the file-based code is small and works; switching storage layers adds risk with no benefit for a single-user bot. Legacy auth-file records without the 'type: oauth' tag must keep working (normalize on read) so the owner never has to re-login after an upgrade. Owner's explicit priority: OAuth must not break on Pi upgrades.

Prompts (prompts/*.txt and the memory/scratchpad preambles) are written for current frontier models: state goals and boundaries once, no repeated tool mechanics, no emphasis like ALL-CAPS or 'VERY important'. Tool descriptions carry the how. Reason: the owner observed the model got confused by hand-holding negative rules (e.g. a 'don't add random crons' instruction caused it to skip crons the owner actually wanted). All behavioural instructions live in the prompt files, not in TypeScript string literals, so they are editable in one place.
